text:
alex: Heads up — seeing a 99th-percentile token latency spike in eu-west when routing falls back to reserved slices. Root cause looks like sticky warmup behavior combined with an outbound egress hotspot. Anyone oncall?

deploy-bot: ALERT eu-west: latency-spike detected · 99p +120ms over baseline · incident=INC-2026-3321

mira: @alex can you paste a trace id or quick logs? :thinking:

alex: trace=abc12345; sample from reserved-slice-7: `warm_affinity=true`, kv-cache-misses spike, connections concentrated on 3 hosts.

sam: looks like the routing heuristic still prefers last-success warm nodes. It keeps priming the same hosts instead of spreading load.

ryan: also seeing NIC tx queue depth climbing on those hosts + small bursty egress to our object cache — could be queue saturation not pure CPU.

mira: two fast mitigations: 1) purge sticky warm-affinity for that slice; 2) apply temporary NIC egress shaping on that slice to spread traffic.

alex: can someone run: `./infractl affinity purge --slice reserved-slice-7 --region eu-west` and then throttle egress?

sam: running now...

sam: output: `ok: 12 active connections drained, affinity-state cleared, new allocations will avoid warm-affinity for 60s`

deploy-bot: ACTION applied · egress-throttle policy p-9987 -> reserved-slice-7 · 250Mbps cap

ryan: after purge + throttle 99p dropped ~90ms, 99.9p still a bit high (~current +200ms). suggests we need either longer cooldown or more capacity.

mira: scaling pool by +1 GPU node would reduce queue pressure. cost impact ~+5% monthly for EU region. We should decide auto-scale vs manual bump.

alex: immediate plan: keep throttle + affinity purge, scale +1 node in eu-west reserved pool. I'll file a follow-up to evaluate auto-scale thresholds and routing heuristic tweak to prefer spread over last-success. Thanks all :thumbsup:
